The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.

But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting. No extant copies could be found.

The debate over the authenticity of the Mecklenburg Declaration began. And, when a copy of a document called the Mecklenburg Resolves written on May 30, 1775, was discovered in a 1775 newspaper, the debate intensified. The Resolves were revolutionary, but stopped short of declaring independence. Did both documents exist? Or was the Declaration being conflated with the Resolves?

Examine the evidence and decide for yourself by visiting the new exhibit, “Mecklenburg Declaration?” at the Presbyterian Heritage Center.

The PHC is open Tuesday-Friday (10-4) and Saturday (12-4).

Eric Debrah Otchere teaches in the Department of Music and Dance (Faculty of Arts, College of Humanities and Legal Studies) at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana. title: The Vijay Iyer Quartet
description:
Some performances—especially jazz—invite you to surrender the need to know what’s coming next. You stop trying to predict the next note and simply hold your breath, waiting to discover where the music will lead. That uncertainty is the thrill: performers and audience alike following the sound somewhere unexpected, until you find yourself wondering, How did they do that?

 

The Vijay Iyer Quartet lives in that space of possibility. Performing compositions by composer-pianist Vijay Iyer, the ensemble reveals new possibilities in the music each time it takes the stage.

 

Voted DownBeat‘s Jazz Artist of the Year four times and a MacArthur Fellow, Iyer has spent decades expanding the possibilities of the jazz quartet. His celebrated trio with bassist Linda May Han Oh and drummer Tyshawn Sorey was praised by The New York Times as “one of the best bands in jazz.”

 

Building on three decades of musical collaboration and experimentation, Iyer expanded the ensemble in 2025 with the addition of trumpeter Adam O’Farrill, a longtime collaborator and member of one of Afro-Latin music’s most revered musical families.

 

Together, the quartet combines acoustic instruments with Fender Rhodes and electronics, creating music that is fearless, unpredictable, and constantly unfolding.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/thevijayiyerquartet/

title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math
description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.

Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. In Practice, you will engage in using math as the building blocks to create art by viewing teacher spotlight videos and exploring exemplar lesson ideas. ShapePatternSymmetryMeasurementCoordinate Points and PlanesRatio/FractionsData VisualizationThe course is aligned with the K–8 North Carolina Standard Course of Study for Visual Art and Math, which can be adapted to support foundational knowledge in secondary art and math courses. title: Hidden Battleship Tour
description:
Offered only four times this coming year, Hidden Battleship takes adventurous visitors beyond the traditional self-guided tour and into unrestored areas of the Battleship North Carolina Memorial that are normally closed to the public. Led by experienced guides in small groups, participants explore spaces deep below deck, throughout the third deck, in the bow, and high into the Ship's superstructure—including all the way to the top.

The 2027 Hidden Battleship tours will be offered on:

Saturday, March 20Saturday, April 24Saturday, November 20Each tour runs from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm. The cost is $75 per participant, plus tax.

Designed for adventurous history enthusiasts, the six-hour experience requires climbing ladders, crossing high hatches, and navigating tight and confined spaces. For that reason, the program is limited to participants ages 16 and older.

Because attendance is intentionally limited to provide a safe, behind-the-scenes experience, Hidden Battleship consistently sells out well in advance. The experience has become a favorite among repeat visitors, military history enthusiasts, photographers, and anyone looking to explore a side of the Ship that few ever have the opportunity to see.

Whether you're searching for a memorable gift or your next great adventure, Hidden Battleship offers an unforgettable behind-the-scenes experience unlike any other.

Visitors are encouraged to reserve their spots early. Tickets and additional information are available at https://bit.ly/hiddenbattleship

title: Che Apalache
description:
What do you get when you blend Appalachian bluegrass and old-time music with Latin American folk traditions including flamenco, murga, and candombe? You get Che Apalache’s acclaimed Latingrass! 

 

Founder Joe Troop grew up in North Carolina and taught music in Buenos Aires after graduating from UNC. His students became his bandmates: Pau Barjau on banjo, Franco Martino on guitar, and Omar Ruiz-Lopez on mandolin.

 

Rooted in traditions that span continents, the band grew out of a willingness to follow interests across languages, cultures, and traditions. What emerged is a sound shaped by relationships, shared experiences, and a genuine openness to learning from one another.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/cheapalache/

title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math
description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.

Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. In Practice, you will engage in using math as the building blocks to create art by viewing teacher spotlight videos and exploring exemplar lesson ideas.  You will reflect on these various projects and select several that connect best with the mathematics standards that you teach, trying out those projects and planning how you would adapt them to your teaching.

The 7 Points of Integration covered in the course are:

ShapePatternSymmetryMeasurementCoordinate Points and PlanesRatio/FractionsData VisualizationThe course is aligned with the K–8 North Carolina Standard Course of Study for Visual Art and Math, which can be adapted to support foundational knowledge in secondary art and math courses. They are open to educators of all disciplines and audiences. A certificate of participation for 10 hours will be provided (1 CEU) with approval from the local school system. The course runs from January 27th - April 6th and educators can join at any point. Registration is now open. $18 Members, $20 Nonmembers.

title: NC Public Librarian Certification Commission
description:
The NC Public Librarian Certification Commission was formed in 1936 to set minimum standards for public librarians to protect and maintain public library resources, to assure professional management and administration of library services, to meet the personnel requirements for State Aid administered by the Library of NC, and to guarantee the best possible public library service to all North Carolinians.

The North Carolina General Statute 143B-68 states that the commission must be comprised of: the Chairman of the public libraries section of NCLA, two individuals named by the Governor upon nomination of the NCLA, the dean of a State or regionally accredited graduate school of librarianship in North Carolina appointed by the Governor, and one member at large appointed by the Governor. Commission members appointed by the Governor serve 4-year terms, all others serve 2-year terms.

Commission meetings are held quarterly to review applications and discuss Certification policies and procedures.

The commission's meeting dates for the 2025-2026 year are October 27, 2025, January 9, 2026, April 10, 2026, and July 10, 2026. All meetings are held at the Library of NC beginning at 1:00 pm unless otherwise posted. Information about meetings can be found on the North Carolina Secretary of State's meeting calendar.

Have questions about certification? Contact us at NC.Certification.Commission@dncr.nc.gov.

title: Forging A Nation: North Carolina in the America Revolution Exhibit
description: This exhibit explores how North Carolina helped forge a new nation during one of the most transformative periods in history. Through maps, historical documents, and everyday objects, this exhibit reveals the state’s role in the struggle for independence, from early protests against British rule and the battles fought on Carolina soil to the drafting of the Constitution. Forging a Nation invites visitors to witness how ordinary people, conflict, and conviction shaped North Carolina's history during the American Revolution.

title: Emanuel Ax, piano & Yo-Yo Ma, cello
description:
To be in the room when Yo-Yo Ma and Emanuel Ax perform together is to witness a musical relationship shaped by more than four decades of friendship, trust, and curiosity. Ax has described their collaboration as one in which the music leads and the musicians follow. Their performances carry an ease and intimacy that only comes from years of listening closely to one another, responding in the moment, and returning again and again to the joy of making music together.

 

What makes this collaboration remarkable is not simply technical mastery. It is the sense of connection that runs through every note. Audiences can hear it in the way one musician follows the other’s lead, anticipates a phrase, or finds space for an unexpected idea to emerge.

 

Both artists are familiar faces at Carolina Performing Arts; Ma through multiple appearances with the Silkroad Ensemble and Ax through recitals and orchestral performances. Experiencing them together offers a rare opportunity to witness two lifelong friends in conversation through music.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/emanuelax-yoyoma/

title: STREB EXTREME ACTION DO NOT TRY THIS AT HOME
description:
What can the human body do? Or maybe, what can it not do?

 

In DO NOT TRY THIS AT HOME, STREB performers—called “Action Heroes”—dive, fling, flip, and fall off of massive moving structures with split-second timing and fearless precision. Audiences gasp, laugh, tense up, and wonder how what they’re seeing is even possible.

 

Founder Elizabeth Streb has been called the Evel Knievel of dance, a thrill-seeker, and a Superwoman. She is the founder of SLAM—the STREB Lab for Action Mechanics—in Brooklyn, where her company has spent decades developing a movement practice called PopAction: a fusion acrobatics, rodeo, dance and athletics, rooted in a lifelong obsession with what happens to the human body when it is fully, fearlessly committed to motion. Her philosophy: “Anything too safe is not action.”

 

The company transforms physical risk into spectacles of wonder, exploring the outer extremes of human movement, asking what becomes possible when courage, creativity, athleticism, and engineering collide.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/streb/

title: Hidden Battleship Tour
description:
Offered only four times this coming year, Hidden Battleship takes adventurous visitors beyond the traditional self-guided tour and into unrestored areas of the Battleship North Carolina Memorial that are normally closed to the public. Led by experienced guides in small groups, participants explore spaces deep below deck, throughout the third deck, in the bow, and high into the Ship's superstructure—including all the way to the top.

The 2027 Hidden Battleship tours will be offered on:

Saturday, February 27Saturday, March 20Saturday, April 24Saturday, November 20Each tour runs from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm. The cost is $75 per participant, plus tax.

Designed for adventurous history enthusiasts, the six-hour experience requires climbing ladders, crossing high hatches, and navigating tight and confined spaces. For that reason, the program is limited to participants ages 16 and older.

"Every compartment aboard the Battleship has a story," said Dr. Jay Martin, Executive Director of Battleship North Carolina Memorial. "Hidden Battleship opens doors that are normally closed, inviting visitors to step into the spaces where sailors lived, worked, and fought—and to experience the Ship in a way very few people ever will."

Because attendance is intentionally limited to provide a safe, behind-the-scenes experience, Hidden Battleship consistently sells out well in advance. The experience has become a favorite among repeat visitors, military history enthusiasts, photographers, and anyone looking to explore a side of the Ship that few ever have the opportunity to see.

Whether you're searching for a memorable gift or your next great adventure, Hidden Battleship offers an unforgettable behind-the-scenes experience unlike any other.

Visitors are encouraged to reserve their spots early. Tickets and additional information are available at https://bit.ly/hiddenbattleship

title: “To BEethoven Rather Than To Seem”: Part V | Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project
description:
FEATURING

Nicholas DiEguenio, violin
Mimi Solomon, piano

 

PROGRAM

Featuring Beethoven’s “Spring” Sonata and Robert Honstein’s Olmsted

This season, Gut Instinct takes on the large-scale project “To Beethoven Rather Than To Seem,” marking 200 years since Beethoven’s death and 250 since the U.S. Declaration of Independence. Over the course of five concerts, Nicholas DiEugenio and pianist Mimi Solomon will present all ten Beethoven Sonatas on period instruments along with five commissioned works written expressly for them.

 

PARKING

Please plan to arrive early as parking on campus can be tricky. Learn more about parking and directions to UNC-Chapel Hill’s campus.

 

The Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project, now in its third season, is a concert series in the Triangle area which brings UNC-Chapel Hill and Duke University’s historical instrument collections together with artists committed to presenting inspired, visceral, historically informed performances of the 19th-century chamber music repertoire. The series features music of female composers and their artistic circles. The name “Gut Instinct” is a play on words. In 19th-century Europe, the violin, viola, and cello were strung with (sheep) gut.

 

All of the artists collaborating with the Pleyel and Graf pianos at UNC-Chapel Hill (built in 19th-century Paris and Vienna, respectively), as well as the Clementi piano at Duke (early 19th-century England) use these gut string materials. The turn of phrase “gut instinct” also refers to the visceral, accessible nature of the musical performances that this series presents. Our mission is to make “Historically Informed Performance” accessible, relatable, and culturally relevant! We also want to feature these special pianos that are rarely heard by the public, along with great music by female composers which has remained lesser known to the greater public for far too long, and living composers who are keeping our art form alive!

The Resolves were revolutionary, but stopped short of declaring independence. Did both documents exist? Or was the Declaration being conflated with the Resolves?

Examine the evidence and decide for yourself by visiting the new exhibit, “Mecklenburg Declaration?” at the Presbyterian Heritage Center.

The PHC is open Tuesday-Friday (10-4) and Saturday (12-4).

title: Battle of Ramsour's Mill
description:
The Battle of Ramsour’s Mill Living History Weekend commemorates the June 20, 1780 Battle of Ramsour’s Mill, when Whigs met Tories on a hillside just outside the little town of Lincolnton.

In 2026, the commemoration will take place the weekend of June 20 & 21 near Battleground Elementary School.

In between, hearth cooking demonstrations by the Lincoln County Hearth Cooks, reenactments and weapons demonstrations, a militia encampment, speakers and storytellers, heritage demonstrations, battleground tours, and period crafts. All activities are free.

Schedule is subject to change. Reenactors and demonstrators welcome! Reenactors who wish to participate should contact Lisa Pupkiewicz at lpupkie@gmail.com; suttlers should contact Beverly Moore at bkingnccp@gmail.com

title: NC Public Librarian Certification Commission
description:
The NC Public Librarian Certification Commission was formed in 1936 to set minimum standards for public librarians to protect and maintain public library resources, to assure professional management and administration of library services, to meet the personnel requirements for State Aid administered by the Library of NC, and to guarantee the best possible public library service to all North Carolinians.

The North Carolina General Statute 143B-68 states that the commission must be comprised of: the Chairman of the public libraries section of NCLA, two individuals named by the Governor upon nomination of the NCLA, the dean of a State or regionally accredited graduate school of librarianship in North Carolina appointed by the Governor, and one member at large appointed by the Governor. Commission members appointed by the Governor serve 4-year terms, all others serve 2-year terms.

Commission meetings are held quarterly to review applications and discuss Certification policies and procedures.

The commission's meeting dates for the 2025-2026 year are October 27, 2025, January 9, 2026, April 10, 2026, and July 10, 2026. All meetings are held at the Library of NC beginning at 1:00 pm unless otherwise posted. Information about meetings can be found on the North Carolina Secretary of State's meeting calendar.

Have questions about certification? Contact us at NC.Certification.Commission@dncr.nc.gov.

title: Building an AI powered, global scale messaging system with XMPP &Deep Learning
description:
Triangle AI Meetup
This talk is an in-depth look at XMPP, the open standard for real-time messaging, and how to build a global scale, AI enhanced messaging system using XMPP. We’ll explore EJabberD, the massively scalable, open-source XMPP server that powers in-game chat for Eve Online, and examine how to: combine XMPP with WebRTC for real-time audio/video calling, add AIML to build helpful chatbots, and how to incorporate Deep Learning to categorize messages in real-time. After the talk, you’ll know how to use XMPP and Ejabberd to build anything from a help-desk chatops application, to a globe spanning in-game messaging system.
